early_blight.name: Early blight
early_blight.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric 'target' rings and a yellow halo, usually starting on older, lower leaves.
tips: Remove and dispose of infected lower leaves.
Water at the base; avoid wetting foliage.
Mulch to stop soil splashing onto leaves.
Rotate crops away from tomato/potato family for 2-3 years.

rust.name: Rust
rust.symptoms: Clusters of small, raised orange-to-brown pustules that rub off as powdery spores, often on leaf undersides.
tips: Pick off and bag affected leaves early.
Improve air circulation by spacing and pruning.
Avoid overhead watering, especially in the evening.

powdery_mildew.name: Powdery mildew
powdery_mildew.symptoms: White to grey powdery patches on the leaf surface that can spread to cover the leaf.
tips: Increase sunlight and airflow around plants.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertiliser, which favours soft growth.
Sulfur or potassium-bicarbonate products are common organic options.

bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial spot
bacterial_spot.symptoms: Many small, dark, angular, water-soaked spots, sometimes with thin yellow halos.
tips: Don't handle plants while they are wet.
Water at soil level; splashing spreads the bacteria.
Sanitise tools and remove badly infected plants.
Use certified disease-free seed and rotate crops.

healthy_info.name: Healthy
healthy_info.symptoms: No disease symptoms detected on the visible leaf area.
tips: Keep monitoring weekly; early detection makes management much easier.

disclaimer: Demo only: this model was trained exclusively on procedurally generated synthetic leaves. It is not an agronomic diagnostic tool; confirm any real diagnosis with a local extension service or plant pathologist.
